public_rationale: The records establish losses at named companies, including Nebius and IREN. They do not establish that every neocloud was deeply unprofitable. Nebius also reports positive adjusted net income, illustrating why the unstated accounting basis matters. That adjusted result is not a counterexample to GAAP net losses. The universal wording and unknown basis prevent a definitive aggregate score.
limitations: Evidence for individual companies cannot establish a universal sector claim.
The qualitative severity term has no supplied threshold.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: CoreWeave, Nebius, IREN and all neoclouds are deeply unprofitable.

statement.excerpt: CoreWeave, Nebius, IREN, and every neocloud is woefully unprofitable, with the justification being that if they just stopped raising money and finished all of these data centers they might one day have positive margins, somehow.

from_speaker: might one day have positive margins
our_interpretation: The ordinary profitability reading is company-level net income after expenses, not EBITDA or gross margin.
Use July–September 2026, the latest quarterly period ordinarily reportable before the November 17 post.
Woefully indicates substantial losses, but supplies no numerical cutoff.
Every neocloud is a universal assertion, not merely a statement about the three named companies.
The sarcastic discussion of possible future margins is not a dated forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable net-income records show substantial losses for the named companies and the defined neocloud population in the target quarter.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A qualifying neocloud reports positive net income on the same accounting basis for the target quarter. Positive EBITDA or adjusted profit alone does not refute a net-income reading.
